glosses: nicht mehr länger an einem Ort anwesend; fort, weg, verschwunden
(als Geschäftsmann, Firma) illiquid, finanziell ruiniert, zahlungsunfähig

examples.text: Die Firma war schon nach einem halben Jahr pleite.
„Damals standen die "Big Three", die drei Giganten der Autoindustrie General Motors, Ford und Chrysler, für den "American Way of Life" schlechthin. Heute sind sie pleite und vom Untergang bedroht.“

glosses: derzeit kein bares Geld besitzend; nur für eine gewisse Zeit mittellos

examples.text: „Man merkt es schon, ich bin pleite und schlecht gelaunt. Die besten Voraussetzungen für den Samstagseinkauf.“
Are they gone already?
The days of my youth are gone.
All the little shops that used to be here are now gone.
I'm afraid all the coffee is gone.

Dust, that a breath could blow aside, yet that was once, like ourselves, animate with hope, passion, and sorrow, is below; around are the vain memorials of human grief and human pride; yet all alike dedicated to the gone.
Have you seen the company's revenue? It's through the floor. They're gone.

glosses: Not fully aware of one's surroundings, often through intoxication or mental decline.

examples.text: Don't bother trying to understand what Grandma says; she's gone.
[S]he put on a kind of sing-song voice whenever she was pissed, it was one of the signs that she was really gone[…].

glosses: Infatuated; in love (+ on, for, in).

examples.text: I am, of course, ‘gone’ for you.
But he was pleased and happy and flattered. She was evidently frightfully gone on him.
It was a group of real gone cats.
“All right, all right, don’t drop your gold all over the place. I have found the gonest little girl in the world and I am going straight to the Lion’s Den with her tonight.”

Six nights gone, your brother fell upon my uncle Stafford, encamped with his host at a village called Oxcross not three days ride from Casterly Rock.

glosses: Weak; faint; feeling a sense of goneness.
Of an arrow: wide of the mark.
Used with a duration to indicate for how long a process has been developing, an action has been performed or a state has persisted; especially, pregnant.

examples.text: She’s three months gone
You'd better hurry up, it's gone four o'clock.

glosses: Alternative spelling of gon /gon': clipping of gonna or going to.

examples.text: Take or be taken. Get yours or get got. It was the code of the streets and I'd lived by it. The way things was looking, I was prolly gone die by it too.
